user.title: Find the heat pump

scan.title: Choose heat pump
scan.description: CTC displays found on Home Assistant's own networks: {count}. Addresses that are already set up are left out.

manual.title: Enter address
manual.description: Type the display's address. It is shown on the panel under Installer, Settings, Communication, Ethernet. Where the display's web interface does not answer, the heat pump is added on Modbus alone: no display pages, no coefficient of performance and no serial number, until the web interface is turned on and the menu is read again under Configure.

modbus_failed.title: Modbus does not answer
modbus_failed.description: The display at {host} answers, but Modbus does not. Turn it on at the panel under Installer, Define, Remote control, where Ethernet must be set to Modbus TCP; the port row only appears once that is done. Then try again, with the same address or a corrected one.

modbus_busy.title: Modbus is taken
modbus_busy.description: The heat pump at {host} accepts a connection on its Modbus port and drops it as soon as anything is asked. The controller takes one Modbus client at a time, and another one holds the place: usually a modbus: block in configuration.yaml pointing at the same unit, a test tool, or a connection that was never let go and that the controller still believes is there. Remove the other client, wait ten minutes, and try again.

slow.title: Slow values from the display
slow.description:
Modbus is read continuously and handles all control. The display's web interface additionally carries values Modbus does not have, such as delivered heat.

The catch is that only the page the panel is showing stays fresh, so the integration has to walk there and back. The panel moves while it does. Tick the pages you want, or skip this step and run on Modbus alone.

The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data, where delivered heat is counted.

{count} pages were found on the {model}; the figure after each is how many values it holds.

From the start, control of the heat pump, the walk to System information, the anonymous statistics and the check for new releases are switched on; all four are changed under Configure. What the statistics send: {privacy_url}

confirm.title: Add {model}?

error.not_a_ctc: That address does not answer as a CTC display. Check the address. The display's web interface is turned on at the panel under Installer, Define, Communication, Web = Yes; without it the heat pump is added on Modbus alone, and then Modbus has to answer.
error.modbus_failed: Modbus did not answer this time either.
error.modbus_transient: Modbus did not answer a moment ago and answers now, so it was a passing hiccup. Try again.
error.modbus_rejected: Something answers on that Modbus TCP port, but not as the heat pump: with a Modbus error, or as a device that does not speak Modbus at all. Check the Modbus TCP port, 502 unless it was changed at the panel, and the Modbus address, normally 1.
error.nothing_found: The search found no CTC display. Type the display's address instead; a display on another network is not reached by the search.
error.only_configured: The search found only displays that are already set up. To add another heat pump, type its display's address; a display on another network is not reached by the search.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: This heat pump is already being added. Finish it from its card under Discovered in Settings, Devices and services, or wait for the other set-up to end.
abort.not_a_ctc: The device is not a CTC display.

data_description.enable_control: Creates control entities that write to CTC's volatile 1000 registers. The controller forgets them about five minutes after the last write, so control releases itself if Home Assistant stops. The stored settings in the 61500 block are never written.
data_description.send_statistics: One report per day to {endpoint}: the integration's version, the Home Assistant version, installation type and Python version, the language and the country you configured in Home Assistant, an approximate position rounded to about 11 km, the number of entities and devices, which transports are in use, whether control is enabled, how many display pages are harvested, how many pages the display's menu has and whether the last reading of the menu since Home Assistant started recognised the home screen and got into the operation data menu, whether the row with the unit's operating hours was recognised on the history page, whether the counters behind the coefficient of performance were found on the display or in Modbus and whether each handed over a number at the last read, and when there is no figure, why: too little energy counted so far, a counter standing still although the unit has been running, or a quotient no heat pump could produce, whether the heat pump's page carries the two power rows at all and whether they handed over numbers at the last read, which a heat pump switched off does not, and whether the figure is worked out from the integration's own sums of the two power readings instead of from the machine's counters. Also the number of failed register reads, the indoor and outdoor unit's model, for an indoor unit the integration does not know yet the family code in the name of the display's settings file (such as ezi4xx, two to sixteen lowercase letters and digits, nothing else), the firmware in the display, the heat pump's control board and the control unit, the product and the year and week of manufacture from the serial number, and the coefficient of performance (COP) over the last day, a rolling year, the machine's first year and the lifetime, the estimated coefficient of performance for today and since the integration began to add it up, and whether it is worked out from the refrigerant circuit. One measurement leaves the house, and only when it is wrong: where a counter stands still or the two counters give an impossible quotient, the two lifetime totals in kilowatt hours are sent along with the flag, never otherwise. Never a name, an address, an exact position, a full serial number, an entity name or a page name, never anything finer than one day, and your IP address is not stored. It also sends a random id created when the integration was installed, so that the daily reports can be kept apart and erased on request (the server keeps it only as a hash, and it says nothing about who you are), a hash that links the beolink plugins running on the same Home Assistant, how many warnings and errors the integration logged since the previous report, and whether it is running or waiting to start again, never the messages themselves or the reason. Switching this off stops the reporting, and the installation is marked as having stopped. What has already been sent stays: it is anonymous, carries no free text and is stored per day, and which installations have existed is what the statistics are for. Erasure on request, from whoever runs the service. The full list: {privacy_url}
data_description.debug_report: Every 30 minutes while it is on, and once when it is switched on, sends what Download diagnostics holds to {endpoint}: every display and Modbus value, how the readings went and when each row was last read, and the integration's own warnings and errors from its log, never a whole traceback. IP addresses, MAC addresses, the serial number's running number and host names are washed out before anything leaves the house, and the server washes them out again. The reports are kept for 14 days and erased on request. Off by default, and independent of the anonymous statistics: the one does not need the other. Switch it off at any time, here or with its switch on the CTC page, which is the same setting. Switching it on or off takes effect at once, without reloading the integration.
data_description.visit_system_info: The panel walks to the display's System information page once and back, to read the serial number and the display's own software version. It presses nothing but Advanced, Display and System information, checks where the panel went after every press, and gives up at the first surprise.
data_description.check_updates: Asks GitHub once a day whether a newer release of this integration exists, and says so in the repairs view. Home Assistant only offers updates for what HACS installed, so a copy put in place by hand is otherwise never offered one.
data_description.slow_pages: The figure after each page is how many values it holds.
data_description.find_page: For a page of the display that the reading of the menu does not reach, such as Kompressor VP1 on an i550 Pro. The next form asks for the page's number, and the search moves the panel, so somebody should stand at the panel.

rescan.title: Slow values from the display
rescan.description: {count} pages were found. The panel was moved during the scan and put back. The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data. The figure after each page is how many values it holds.

find_page.title: Search for the way to a page
find_page.description: The search moves the panel in the plant room, so somebody should stand at the panel while it runs. From the operation data menu's root it tries at most {taps} controls, at most {depth} presses deep, stops at the page, records the way there, reads the page and puts the panel back where it was, or on the home screen where it does not know the way back. It never presses anything in Service, Define or the language selection, nothing in a page's heading but the panel's own button, never that button on the home screen, and nothing outside the operation data menu but that button, to leave it. The page's number is in the display's screen map, {screen_map}, the number before each colon. Or walk the panel to the page by hand: the field is filled in with the page the panel shows right now.

data_description.page: The number before a colon in the screen map, or the page the panel shows.

find_page_found.title: Page found
find_page_found.description: Page {page}, {title}, is {steps} presses from the operation data menu's root and was found after {tries} tries. It holds {count} values, and the panel is back where it was, or on the home screen. Submit to add the page to the menu, ticked, so it is read with the other pages; close the dialog and nothing is saved.

error.panel_busy: The panel is in use right now: the integration is reading the display's pages or walking its menu. Try again in a moment.
error.page_unknown: The display's screen map has no page with that number.
error.page_outside: That page is the home screen or a page of a menu the search stays out of, so it was not searched for. Nothing has been saved.
error.no_menu: The operation data menu could not be found on the panel, so nothing in it was pressed. Nothing has been saved.
error.page_not_found: The page was not found within the search's limits, so the way there cannot be reached from the operation data menu just now. An i550 Pro draws the way to some pages only in some operating states, so it may be worth trying again once the operating state has changed. Nothing has been saved, and the panel stands where it was or on the home screen.
error.page_lost: The search lost its way back in the menu and stopped. Nothing has been saved. Look at the panel: it may not be where it was.
error.page_empty: The page was found but holds no value to read. Nothing has been saved.
error.page_gap: The page was found but could not be read whole: a screen or a caption did not answer. Nothing has been saved; try again in a moment.
error.display_silent: The display stopped answering during the search. Nothing has been saved.

abort.panel_busy: The panel is in use right now: the integration is reading the display's pages or walking its menu. Try again in a moment. Nothing has been changed.
abort.one_walk: Tick either Read the display's menu again or Search for the way to a page, not both: each of them moves the panel. Nothing has been changed.

pages_unticked.title: No page of the display is ticked
pages_unticked.description: The display's menu has been read, but not one of its pages is ticked, so the display is never read: delivered heat, and with it the coefficient of performance, lives only there. Tick the pages under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure. The coefficient of performance needs the page with the stored or historical operation data.

menu_unread.title: The display's menu could not be read
menu_unread.description: No page of the display is read, because its menu could not be read: the integration did not find its way from the home screen into the operation data menu, or the display did not answer. Until then only Modbus is read, without delivered heat or a coefficient of performance. The menu is tried again three times, five minutes apart, after every start of Home Assistant, and at once with Read the display's menu again under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure. If it never works, download the diagnostics from the integration's menu and attach them to an issue on GitHub: they show how far the reading got.

history_page_missing.title: The coefficient of performance is missing its history page
history_page_missing.description: The coefficient of performance is worked out from the display's counter for delivered heat, which lives on the page with the stored or historical operation data. That page is not being read. Tick it under Settings, Devices and services, CTC Local Easyconf, Configure.

identity_incomplete.title: The serial number has not been read
identity_incomplete.description: The display writes the serial number and its own software version into the System information page only once that page has been shown on the panel. Open it once on the panel, or let the integration walk there itself under Configure.

modbus_busy.title: Another client holds the heat pump's Modbus connection
modbus_busy.description: The controller takes one Modbus client at a time. It accepts this integration's connection and drops it as soon as anything is asked, which is how it says that another client holds the place: a modbus: block in configuration.yaml pointing at the same unit, a test tool, or a session that was never let go. Remove the other client and wait ten minutes. The integration keeps trying by itself, and this notice goes at the first reading that works.

update_available.title: A newer version of CTC Local Easyconf is out
update_available.description: Version {latest} has been released; this is {installed}. Installed through HACS: update it there, under Settings, Devices and services, HACS. Installed by hand: replace custom_components/ctc_ecozenith with the new release and restart Home Assistant.

modbus_busy.message: Another client holds the heat pump's only Modbus connection; see the repairs view

modbus_closed.message: The heat pump does not accept a connection on its Modbus port: it is switched off or out of reach, the address is wrong, or Modbus TCP is off at the panel

not_a_control.message: {entity_id} is not a control of a loaded CTC Local Easyconf heat pump, so there is nothing to release

unknown_entry.message: {entry_id} is not a CTC Local Easyconf heat pump

no_display.message: {entry} was set up on Modbus alone and has no display menu to read

no_display_loaded.message: No loaded heat pump has a display menu to read

panel_busy.message: The panel of {entries} is in use right now: the integration is reading the display's pages or walking its menu. Try again in a moment. Nothing has been changed.

menu_not_read.message: The display's whole menu of {entries} could not be read, so the stored menu stands and nothing has been changed

menu_busy_and_not_read.message: The panel of {busy} is in use right now, and the display's whole menu of {missed} could not be read, so the stored menu stands. Try again in a moment. Nothing has been changed.

menu_partly_read.message: The display's menu was read again on only some of the heat pumps. Read whole and saved, the heat pump reloads: {read}. Panel in use right now, try again in a moment: {busy}. Menu not read whole, the stored menu stands: {missed}.

no_counters.message: {entry} has no energy counters among the display pages it reads, so there is no coefficient of performance to sample

no_counters_loaded.message: No loaded heat pump has the energy counters the coefficient of performance is worked out from

release.name: Release control
release.description: Stops Home Assistant holding the given controls, without writing anything to the heat pump. The heat pump goes back to its own setting within about five minutes, when it forgets the last write. Other controls stay as they are.

entity_id.name: Controls
entity_id.description: The number or select entities of this integration to release.

reread_menu.name: Read the display's menu again
reread_menu.description: Walks the display's menu once, as Read the display's menu again in the integration's options does, and folds the pages it finds into the stored menu: a page that is switched off stays off, and a new page is read from then on. Moves the physical panel and puts it back. A panel that is in use right now is not waited for.

config_entry_id.name: Heat pump
config_entry_id.description: Which heat pump. Leave out for every heat pump with a display.

cop_sample.name: Take a sample of the coefficient of performance
cop_sample.description: Writes down the two lifetime energy counters, as they stood when the display was last read, as a sample of the coefficient of performance now rather than at the next six hourly sample, and answers with the counters. A reading that is already a sample is not taken twice.

config_entry_id.name: Heat pump
config_entry_id.description: Which heat pump. Leave out for every heat pump with the energy counters.

compressor_hours_24h.name: Compressor running time over the last day

hp1_outdoor_temp.name: Outdoor temperature at the heat pump

hp_fw.name: Heat pump control board software version

mean_run_24h.name: Mean run over the last day

debug_report.name: Report all values to the developer
